Where to Stay in Phitsanulok?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Phitsanulok hotels across every budget — from a Nan River boutique and a 4-star downtown hotel to value city stays and a vintage dorm from ฿350/night. Covering the main areas: the Nan riverside, the Wat Yai temple area and downtown. From roughly ฿350–2,500/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Phitsanulok matter?
introHtml: Phitsanulok is a town on the Nan River, and the main draw for most visitors is Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai), home to Phra Buddha Chinnarat — a Buddha image many regard as one of the most beautiful in Thailand. Stays fall broadly into three areas: the Nan riverside suits anyone wanting water views and a quiet feel, with several places a short walk or drive from Wat Yai and the riverside market; the Wat Yai area lets you easily walk to pay respects to Phra Buddha Chinnarat and browse the markets; and downtown (Mittraphap Road, Akathodsarot Road, near Central and Topland malls) is easy to get around, close to the train station and restaurants, and ideal as a base before continuing to Sukhothai or Khao Kho. Phitsanulok is a lower-northern transport hub, so many people overnight here in transit — picking an area near what you want to see saves real time. This guide rounds up 12 Phitsanulok hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Phitsanulok has no metro, but it's a key transport hub for the lower north — there's a central railway station (Northern Line, Bangkok–Chiang Mai, every train stops here), Phitsanulok Airport (PHS) about 5 km from town, and a bus terminal connecting Sukhothai, Khao Kho, Phetchabun and nearby provinces. In town you can grab a taxi, rent a car or take a songthaew easily. The areas in this guide: Nan riverside — water views, a quiet feel, near Wat Yai and the riverside market · Wat Yai area — walk to pay respects to Phra Buddha Chinnarat and browse markets · downtown — Mittraphap and Akathodsarot Roads, near the train station, Central and Topland malls, easiest access.

entries.storyHtml: Topland is a large 4-star downtown hotel connected directly to Topland Mall, and the most-reviewed property in this guide — 185 reviews, score 8.8. The draw is a central location where you can take the lift straight into the mall, close to the Nan River and Wat Yai, with bathtubs in the rooms and Family Suites for groups. Real guest reviews praise the location and the range of facilities, but note it's a long-established hotel and parts are showing their age, so ask for a renovated room. Best for those wanting a full-service downtown hotel and easy shopping.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a newer room with a city view, ask for a renovated higher floor. With the mall attached, you can shop and find food without going outside even when it rains.

Best for those wanting a clean, well-priced room for a quick overnight or as a sightseeing base.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Phitsanulok hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in within Phitsanulok?
faq.a: It depends on your style. The Nan riverside suits those wanting water views and a quiet feel, near Wat Yai (The Grand Riverside, Yodia Heritage, Dragon River, Wangchan Riverview). Downtown is easy to get around, near the train station, Central and Topland malls (Topland, Fortune D, Hop Inn, Holatel, Morage, Amarinnakhon). For budget/dorm stays, The 8 Factory Hostel and Sendee Hostel suit backpackers and solo travellers.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Phitsanulok hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and value stays from around ฿350–490/night · midrange and budget city hotels around ฿650–950 · riverside boutiques and 4-star hotels around ฿1,100–1,500 · an upscale riverside boutique like Yodia Heritage from around ฿2,500. All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms; during festivals and long weekends rates are higher and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay near Wat Yai (Phra Buddha Chinnarat)?
faq.a: Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai), home to Phra Buddha Chinnarat, sits on the Nan River. Several riverside stays in this guide are a short walk or ride from paying respects — Yodia Heritage, Dragon River Avenue and Wangchan Riverview are all on the river near Wat Yai. On a budget there's Sendee Hostel, in town near Wat Yai and the train station.

faq.q: ❓ Arriving by train — which hotel is near the station?
faq.a: Phitsanulok train station is downtown. Amarinnakhon Hotel sits right opposite it — just cross the road — ideal for late arrivals or early departures. Morage Phitsanulok and The Grand Riverside are also near the station, a short walk or ride away. The 8 Factory Hostel is near both the airport and the train station.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Phitsanulok hotel?
faq.a: On weekdays outside festival periods, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But over long weekends, New Year, Songkran and merit-making events around Phra Buddha Chinnarat, rooms fill fast and prices rise, so book 2–4 weeks ahead. Phitsanulok is a hub where people overnight en route to Sukhothai, Khao Kho and Phetchabun, so the high seasons of nearby destinations can fill town rooms faster too.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking a Phitsanulok hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so we recommend comparing all 3 before every booking — each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night, especially on riverside boutiques and 4-star hotels during festivals.
